description: A euclidean sequencer that spreads a number of active steps around a ring of up to 32, with accents, rotation and padding, and four ways of placing the steps

params.text: Sets how many steps the pattern holds, 1 to 32; it comes up at 16
Sets how many of the pattern's steps are active, read as a fraction of the LENGTH: one step at the bottom of the knob and every step at the top
Turns the whole pattern clockwise, carrying triggers and accents together, from no shift up to one step short of a full turn
Moves the accents round among the active steps, from no shift up to one short of the number of active steps
Adds inactive steps after the pattern, enough to fill 32 steps in all, which pushes the active steps out of their even spacing
Sets how many of the active steps are accented, from none up to all of them
Cycles through the four ways of placing the active steps — Euclidean, Random, Fibonacci and Linear — and recolours itself and the display to match
Cycles the GATE output through Trigger, Gate and Turing
Runs the pattern counter-clockwise; the panel prints RV

inputs.text: Shifts the number of active steps; the voltage is divided by 9 and added to the STEPS knob
Shifts the LENGTH: 10V adds 31 steps and -10V takes 31 away, the total held between 1 and 32
Shifts the pattern rotation; the voltage is divided by 9 and added to the ROT knob
Shifts the accent rotation; the voltage is divided by 9 and added to the ACC ROT knob
Shifts the accent count; the voltage is divided by 9 and added to the ACC knob
Shifts the padding; the voltage is divided by 9 and added to the PAD knob
A rising edge advances the pattern by one step
A trigger sets the pattern back to its first step

outputs.text: In Trigger mode a 1ms 10V pulse on each active step, in Gate mode 10V held from an active step until an inactive one, and in Turing mode a voltage read off the whole pattern as a binary number
A 10V trigger or gate on each active step that is also an accent, following the gate mode; in Turing mode a 1ms 10V pulse on every active step
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the pattern comes back round to its first step

notes: Nothing moves until a clock is patched: the pattern only advances on a rising edge at the clock input.
The display draws the pattern as a ring of circles, active steps bright on the inner ring and accents promoted to the outer one, with the current step drawn larger.
The reverse button is the one control the maker left unnamed, so hovering it shows no tooltip.
